title: Selected Topics in Law and Society; Social Injustice in Flint, Newark, and Baltimore
description:
What environmental conditions look like at the local level raises justice concerns involving race, gender, age and economic situation. In this course, we'll consider how the law has or has not addressed environmental conditions in a variety of localities. For example, the Flint water crisis meant that the municipal water system failed to protect residents from lead in the water. As a result, among other things, thousands of young children experienced insults to their brains that may impact their education and opportunities over their lifetimes. We wil examine how special education law (Individuals with Disabilities Education Act) may or may not improve the lives of the children, their families and their community.

Students will be expected to attend and participate in class, complete two writing assignments each week, and investigate an environmental issue affecting a local community.
